preview: An interview experience for an Internship at Morgan Stanley via the App Dev track, detailing the online test and subsequent technical and HR rounds.
content:
INTERVIEW EXPERIENCE(Internship)
MORGAN STANLEY
Dhruvin Gandhi- B Tech CS-(2019-2023)
Overview: (3rd September- Online test, 6th September- Interviews)
Eligibility Criteria: 7.5+ CGPA
They provide 2 tracks: Application Development (App dev) and Enterprise Engineering Track (EE)
EE track focuses more on subjects like OS,DBMS whereas App Dev focuses more on Data structures and algorithms.
I had selected the App Dev track.
●Round 1(Online Test)
The online test was conducted on the AMCAT platform and the test had mainly three sections.
1. Aptitude Section(20 mins,10questions)-
It had mainly MCQs on topics like probability,PnC,Time and work,Pipes and Cistern and some statistics.
Questions weren’t difficult but the time provided was less.Hence, developing speed is necessary.
https://www.indiabix.com/aptitude/questions-and-answers/
I was not able to solve 3-4 questions due to the time limit.
2. Debugging Section(20 mins,7 questions)-
There were 7 questions where we had to select a programming language out of C/C++/Java and questions were mainly based on logical errors and syntax errors. So we had to correct that so that the desired output is produced.
For eg:-
int solve(int arr[],int n)
{
int res=0;
for(int i=0;i<n;i++)
{
res=res*arr[i];
}
return res;
}
You have to correct the code so that the desired output is produced.
I was not able to solve 2 questions due to the time limit.
3. Coding Section(60 mins,3 questions)-
The questions were not direct but had a long story related to it.
You just have to find the useful information from the question.
1. https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-valid-parentheses/
2. https://leetcode.com/problems/merge-intervals/
3. The third question was a very simple dp problem.
I was able to solve all the three questions in 45 mins.
So this was the online round.
App Dev Track:- 25 were shortlisted
EE track:- 13 were shortlisted
●Round 2(Technical Round,75 mins)
The interview started with him introducing himself followed by a Tell me about yourself question.
After that he asked me about my recent project in which I had used Object Oriented Programming.
Based on my answer he told me to code a few classes in notepad.
Then he told me to do an oop design of the parking lot system.
https://crack-oop-system-design.herokuapp.com/
Here you can find the commonly asked oop design questions.
Based on the discussion we had about the parking lot:-
1. What are use cases of the parking lot?
2. Asked me to write the class for a single parking space and a parking lot.
3. Asked me to write the class for a vehicle.
4. What oop concept would most likely to be used here like (Inheritance,Polymorphism)
5. What data structure should be used so as to get the nearest free parking space from the entry point?
I told a min heap would be the best data structure to store the free parking spaces and he was satisfied with the answer.
He also asked me concepts like abstraction and polymorphism and what is the difference between overriding and overloading.
After this he asked me:-
1. You are given large chunks of data of share prices and your task is to sort them. What sorting algorithm would you use?
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/external-sorting/
2. You are given a nearly sorted array. What sorting algorithm would you use?
3. Based on my answer in the first question he asked me what is the other feature that merge sort offers?
Ans:- stability
Based on my oop design he asked me why I had used vectors instead of arrays and asked me the difference between the two.
Based on my answer he asked me when you initialize a vector or array where does that memory allocate.
Then he asked me about Memory heaps and stacks.
Then he said that he was trying to allocate a large size array/vector but he was getting an error saying that the memory limit had been exceeded.
He asked me what could be the possible reason for this and how can you solve it.
He gave me a hint for this question based on which I was able to answer correctly.
Reason:- finding a large contiguous memory for array or vector can lead to memory limit exceeded.
Linked lists can be used to solve the error.
Later he told me to code and explain the following in notepad(also did a dry run of few test cases):-
1. Reverse a linked list
2. Quick sort
3. A simple dp problem
I wasn't asked a single question about os /dbms however other candidates were asked.
He was quite satisfied with the solutions. He then asked me if I had any questions.(Always ask something, it shows that you are interested)
He was very friendly and discussed with me the projects he works on and other opportunities at Morgan Stanley.
App Dev Track:- 12 were shortlisted
EE track:- 4 were shortlisted
Round 3(HR + Technical Round,45 mins)
Again I was asked About Introducing myself and he asked to
●Describe one of the projects that I had mentioned in my resume and also asked about my internship.
●Based on my internship he asked me a few questions about python.
●You have built an application and a user has reported a certain problem. What would be your step by step approach to solve the problem?
Then Some HR questions were asked:
●What difficulties/challenges did you face while doing a group project?
●Describe a situation where your teammates were convinced to go with your idea and how did you convince them
●Describe a situation where you were not satisfied with the work you have done and what did you do then?
After a few more hr questions he asked me if I had any questions for him.
(Ask questions always).
In the end around 9:30/10:00 the same night the results came, 11 of us were selected (2 EE, 9 App dev).
